raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw DG $\perp$ AC at G, and draw EH $\perp$ AC at H, \\
then $\angle$DGM=$\angle$MHE=$90^\circ$, \\
in $\triangle ABC$, $BC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-AC^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-8^{2}}=6$, \\
since D is the midpoint of AB, \\
thus AD=$\frac{1}{2}$AB=5, \\
since $\angle$AGD=$\angle$ACB=$90^\circ$, $\angle$DAG=$\angle$BAC, \\
thus $\triangle ADG\sim \triangle ABC$, \\
thus $\frac{DG}{BC}=\frac{AG}{AC}=\frac{AD}{AB}$, that is $\frac{DG}{6}=\frac{AG}{8}=\frac{5}{10}$, \\
thus DG=3, AG=4, \\
thus CG=AC−AG=8−4=4, \\
since the area of $\triangle MDF$ is $\sqrt{3}$ times the area of $\triangle MEF$, \\
thus $\frac{1}{2}$FM•DG=$\sqrt{3} \times \frac{1}{2}$FM•EH, \\
thus DG=$\sqrt{3}$EH, that is EH=$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$DG=$\sqrt{3}$, \\
in $\triangle DEM$, $\angle$DME=$90^\circ$, $\angle$DEM=$30^\circ$, \\
thus $\frac{DM}{ME}=\tan\angle DEM=\tan30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$, \\
since $\angle$DMG+$\angle$MDG=$90^\circ$, $\angle$DMG+$\angle$EMH=$\angle$DME=$90^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle$MDG=$\angle$EMH, \\
thus $\triangle DMG\sim \triangle MEH$, \\
thus $\frac{MG}{EH}=\frac{DM}{ME}$, \\
thus $\frac{MG}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$, \\
thus MG=1, \\
thus CM=CG+MG=4+1=\boxed{5},
